Context/Background: UBE2M, an essential neddylation E2 enzyme, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of various diseases, including cancers, viral infections, and obesity. However, whether UBE2M is involved in the pathogenesis of bacterial sepsis remains unclear. In an Escherichia coli (E. coli)-induced sepsis mouse model, increased UBE2M expression in macrophages in liver and lung tissues postinfection was observed. To further clarify the role of UBE2M in macrophages, mice with macrophage-specific deletion of UBE2M were constructed.
Prompt: We isolated and purified peritoneal macrophages (PMs) from control mice and mice with UBE2M deletion.  We then stimulated PMs with Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) (to mimic infection) and performed RNASeq.  Based on the differential expression analysis between PMS of control (WL) vs UBE2M deletion (KL) mice under LPS stimulation, please provide a discussion of the genes and affected pathways as relates to UBE2M deletion in the context of bacterial sepsis.
output_text:
**Introduction/Context**  
Peritoneal macrophages (PMs) were isolated from control (WL) and macrophage-specific UBE2M-deleted (KL) mice. Following LPS stimulation to mimic bacterial infection, RNA-seq was performed (geneID counts for KL1–3 vs WL1–3; raw counts, not specified replicates). Differential expression (DESeq2-GSEA & ORA) contrasted KL vs WL under LPS. Key findings: cytokine signaling (↑), cell-cycle (↑), redox/metabolism (↓) pathways.

**Keywords**  
• Neddylation  
• Cytokine signaling  
• Cell-cycle  
• Inflammatory response  
• Oxidative metabolism  

**Candidate Genes**  
UBE2M, NEDD8, NFKB1, IL6, TNF, IL1B, SOCS3, CXCL10

**Pathway Enrichments**  

Overall Up/Down ratios (counts_by_database):  
• KEGG_2016  32↑/31↓ (51%↑; ratio 1.03)  
• GO_BP_2023 317↑/95↓ (77%↑; ratio 3.34)  
• Reactome_2024 97↑/103↓ (49%↑; ratio 0.94)  
• MSigDB_Hallmark 12↑/10↓ (55%↑; ratio 1.20)

KEGG_2016 (UP):  
| Theme                                      | Direction | Leading Genes (subset)                            |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------|
| Cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction     | UP        | IL6; IL1B; TNFSF10; CXCL10; CSF3; IL12B…          |
| Jak-STAT signaling pathway                 | UP        | IL6; IL1B; STAT3; SOCS1; SOCS3; CSF2…             |

KEGG_2016 (DOWN):  
| Theme                                      | Direction | Leading Genes                                  |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Glutathione metabolism                     | DOWN      | GCLM; GCLC; GSTA2; GPX4; GSS…                   |

GO_BP_2023 (UP):  
| Theme                                      | Direction | Leading Genes                              |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------|
| Inflammatory Response                      | UP        | IL6; IL1B; NFKB1; CCL2; CXCL10; CSF2…      |
| Mitotic Sister Chromatid Segregation       | UP        | ESPL1; KIF2C; SMC2; PLK1; BIRC5…           |

GO_BP_2023 (DOWN):  
| Theme                                      | Direction | Leading Genes                              |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------|
| Inorganic Cation Import Across Plasma Membrane | DOWN      | ATP1A1; CACNA1C; KCNJ2…                    |

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (UP):  
| Theme                                      | Direction | Leading Genes                              |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------|
| Mitotic Spindle Checkpoint                 | UP        | BUB1; MAD2L1; NDC80; UBE2C; AURKB…         |

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (DOWN):  
| Theme                                      | Direction | Leading Genes                              |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------|
| Biological Oxidations                      | DOWN      | GCLM; GSTA2; GSTO1; ALDH2; CYP11A1…         |

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP):  
| Theme                                      | Direction | Leading Genes                              |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------|
| G2-M Checkpoint                            | UP        | CCNB1; CDK1; BUB1; PLK1; UBE2C…            |
| Interferon Gamma Response                  | UP        | NFKB1; STAT1; CXCL10; IFIT1; IRF1…         |

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN):  
| Theme                                      | Direction | Leading Genes                              |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------|
| Apoptosis                                  | DOWN      | CASP7; BCL2L11; CDKN1B; TNFSF10; IL1B…      |

Analysis: UBE2M deletion under LPS markedly enhances pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine signaling (KEGG cytokine-receptor, JAK-STAT; GO inflammatory response) and cell-cycle/mitotic programs (GO mitotic segregation; Reactome spindle, MSigDB G2-M). Conversely, redox/metabolic (glutathione metabolism, biological oxidations) and apoptotic pathways are suppressed. The balanced up/down GSEA ratio in KEGG (~1.0) shifts toward upregulated immune/stress modules in GO/MSigDB.

**Targeted (keyword-guided) subset**  
Filtering ORA (MSigDB_Hallmark) for “TNF” terms:  
| Term                                   | Adj P-val         | Genes (subset)                     |
|----------------------------------------|-------------------|-------------------------------------|
| TNF-alpha Signaling via NF-kB          | 4.44e-34          | IL6; IL1B; NFKB1; CXCL10; CSF2…     |
| TNF signaling pathway                  | 1.12e-10¹         | IL6; IL1B; NFKB1; CCL2; PTGS2…      |

These confirm robust TNF-NFκB axis engagement in UBE2M-deficient PMs after LPS.

**Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)**  

Up (Cytokine/Inflammation):  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                        | Pathway(s)                             |
|--------|-----------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| IL6    | Up        | Pro-inflammatory cytokine            | TNF-NFκB, JAK-STAT, Inflammatory Resp. |
| IL1B   | Up        | Pro-inflammatory cytokine            | TNF-NFκB, Cytokine Receptor            |
| NFKB1  | Up        | Transcription factor (NF-κB subunit) | TNF-NFκB, Interferon Gamma Response   |
| CCL2   | Up        | Monocyte chemoattractant             | Inflammatory Response                 |
| CXCL10 | Up        | Chemokine, T-cell/NK recruitment     | Cytokine Receptor, IFNγ Response      |
| SOCS3  | Up        | Negative regulator of JAK-STAT       | JAK-STAT signaling                    |

Down (Redox/Metabolism):  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                        | Pathway(s)                             |
|--------|-----------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| GCLM   | Down      | Glutathione biosynthesis             | Glutathione metabolism, Oxidations     |
| GSTA2  | Down      | Glutathione S-transferase            | Glutathione metabolism                 |
| ALDH2  | Down      | Aldehyde detoxification              | Oxidations, Pyruvate metabolism        |
| CYP11A1| Down      | Steroid biosynthesis                 | Biological Oxidations, Steroid biosyn. |

UBE2M itself: “not observed” in DE outputs (geneID ENSMUSG00000000001; counts KL_sum 7846 vs WL_sum 7302; change not significant).

**Comparisons**  
Peritoneal PMs show concordant upregulation of cytokine/inflammatory modules and cell-cycle pathways, with metabolic suppression. No tissue-specific proteomics provided for cross-validation.

**Implications**  
UBE2M deletion augments LPS-driven pro-inflammatory and proliferative signaling in PMs while impairing antioxidant metabolism. In sepsis, this may exacerbate cytokine storm and impair redox homeostasis—suggesting neddylation as a check on macrophage hyperactivation.

**Next Steps & Clarification**  
1. Validate DE of UBE2M by qPCR/protein in PMs (counts show minimal DE).  
2. Assess ROS levels and GSH/GSSG ratio in KL vs WL PMs post-LPS to confirm metabolic findings.  
3. Test functional cytokine release (IL-6, IL-1β, TNF) by ELISA.  
4. Examine impact of UBE2M loss on NF-κB activation kinetics (phospho-p65).

References  
No PMIDs validated via Steps 5–6 directly for UBE2M in bacterial sepsis macrophages; omitted.
